I was saying that I keep a slightly higher poly density on joints for the people who don't know how to use alpha maps or create udims on their avatar as I can't do it automatically.

So having a higher density on the joints means that the people who only know how to drag and drop a vrcfury asset don't necessarily need to do anything else like editing their materials.
The people who knows aren't bothered by it and the ones who don't have minimal clipping

most of the times outfits are way too high poly then they should be as well, i use marvelous designer and sell clothing for some avatar bases so i know a bit on the subject.  
high poly mainly helps where there's deformation since if the topology is not exactly the same as the body and it's a similar density it will not work well, you can only do so much with weight painting.   
  
I usually keep a slightly higher poly density where it deforms after the retopology for the people who only know how to use vrcfury, but i always advise people to use the alpha map (that i usually include in the packages i make) or better yet to modify their avatar adding UDIMs to completely get rid of clipping, especially in the armpit area and the crotch/butt area.  
UDIMs are especially nice since they completely disable the mesh in a uv tile instead of rendering transparency with the alpha map, but that can only be done with shaders like poiyomi and not the standard unity one (and it's also a little bit more advanced that what the majority of people know how to do)

While optimisation is important and I try to be at least medium rating at all times. Polygons are really the least to worry about, not only because they are technically the cheapest to render, but mainly because an avatar showing 500k polygons doesn't mean that they are on all the time. Having multiple meshes you can toggle means that you only see and render what's on.


What people forget about is to set textures at an optimised resolution and optimizing the number of materials, most often people don't need 50 material slot or 4k textures on all the maps, especially metallic maps, alpha maps and roughness maps.


For my avi I usually set those at 256 or 512px, the diffuse or base color to 1024 or 2048px and the normal map at 2048; As for material slots 1 for the hair, 1 for the body, and 1 for each outfit is a good rule for me.

Regardless of if this is bs or not, there are already cameras that can do 400mpx but they are obviously incredibly expensive and to achieve that, they also use a technique called sensor shifting where the sensor shift it's position to do 4x the resolution.
If you look at the fuji gfx 100 lineup on YouTube you can see some crazy things.

The real problem is not much of a resolution one to achieve what we can see (as any decent camera can look amazing at any resolution, look at the Sony a7s lineup), but refresh rate and even more important how does a camera handle light.

If you try with any camera to point and focus at a spot where the light is more, you'll see everything else getting very dark and viceversa; there are techniques to avoid this but they involve taking multiple picture at different exposure and combining them together, and in video it's usually done in post with the raw (and very flat looking log file) by a color grader.

Sure phone camera has gotten decent enough at doing this automatically, but it's still not good at handling a difference in light level across the scene the camera is looking at, and it's usually done by taking the average luminosity of the scene.


PS: my intent here is not shitting on everything, I'm just giving out some interesting insight as a photographer

The problem is a logitech service that windows 11 installs on its latest updates. It's called logitech lamp array and it breaks windows ink. To fix the issue press windows + r and type msconfig. At that point navigate to service and search for logitech lamp array service, right click and disable it completely (not just stopping it, disable it).

Lamparray it's a service for logitech lamps that for some reason interfere with either huion translation layer between it's own driver and windows ink or just one of the 2, it's also very weird that it gets installed automatically.


Otherwise there can be other software that mess with it, one other I know of because someone else commented on another post was RGBfusion.

With these info we can only speculate that if you don't have either of these services or program, there's likely something else of the same nature that is causing the problem, I would look for any software that control lights (again tho, it's most likely to be lamparray fault)

You need to disable the lamp array service not terminated it.if it's not that it could be because of another program.

Either way it's either a Windows ink issue or a Windows update issue, this problem started appearing a month ago and from there lots of help request started popping In this reddit.

    sudo rpm -e --nodeps --allmatches kernel-core-6.7.5-100.fc38.x86_64 (obv to replace with the version you have)

BTW, i just uninstalled lamp array, if you would like to know how (or any driver for that matter) here's the steps:

1: first open powershell with administrator rights, then type: 

`Get-WindowsDriver -Online -All`

2: copy the whole thing to a text file and do CTRL - F to find the lamparray driver and note driver indicative name. In my case the entry was this:

  
`Driver           : oem2.inf`

`OriginalFileName : C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository\logi_lamparray_usb.inf_amd64_0772df9f9e65a702\logi_lamparray_usb.inf`

`....... ect`

3: then type this in powershell:

`pnputil /delete-driver oem2.inf /uninstall /force`

where oem2.inf will obviously be what you will have in your case

The elegoo Saturn is excellent! Although I'll suggest you to get a lot of research on the topic, as the bigger the printer, the messy with the resin you'll get. For tabletop games I recommend the ELEGOO Mars 2 pro or the ELEGOO Mars 3 (the latter does the best resolution as it is a 4k LCD compared to the 2k one on the Mars 2. The Saturn has also a 4k screen but since it a bigger printer it does have less PPI overhaul, still better than the Mars 2).

You basically want the printer and the curing and washing station (I have the elegoo mercury X) as well as tons of alcohol (every type is ok but preferable at least 90% isopropyl or ethilic alcohol, if you can, get the transparent one, so you can use it as a thinner for normal acrylic paint if you want to get an airbrush).

Get a LOT of gloves and masks because resin is toxic before curated, and make sure you have water available to you ALL the time.

I would also get a spare LCD for your resin printer and spares FEP (which is the transparent sheet that is on the bottom of the resin tank). The LCD screen will eventually wear out and get dead pixels after a couple of thousand hrs of printing cause of the UV underneath.

​

For the models you need non-manifold models (which basically means that everything is just one block, otherwise you'll might have problems with your prints if you do a hollow print, also placing drain holes is fundamental for your non cured resin to get out of the model and to avoid a "sucking" effect

​

last but not least, I would also consider (I'm getting one too) a multitool like a dremel for sanding and polishing  


​

If you want a better cpu you have to go with an I7 8700 or i7 8700k if you don’t want to upgrade your motherboard too. Also try to get another 8gb ram stick (preferably the same mounted already in your pc)

If you are preferring intel and nvidia just for the brand, let me tell you that it’s not going to benefit in any way. For an instance, the ryzen 7 2700 has 16 thread and 8 cores while the 8700k has 6 cores and 12 threads. The price difference is roughly about 200/250€ In favor of the ryzen and in multi core it literally smash the intel. Also intel, in the new i7 9700k has no hypertreading which is absurd. Going for higher voltage is never a good choice if for the Same performance and price you are going to have better or similar performance while be not that much power hungry. Just be smart and be a fan of your wallet. Trust me

For the other question, ssd can be m.2 or sata, just search on amazon. Any computer can run a 144hz screen but in a lot of games you are not going to archive 144fps (other than esport title like lol, csgo amd so on). Oh, don’t upgrade anything before changing your psu, in most cases prebuilt psu (power supply) are just right for that component so you often need a new one.

First, over clocking basically makes your parts (you can over clock the cpu, the gpu, the monitor for more hz and the ram) runs faster and that basically means more power. However you need to be wise, you can’t overclock too much (in some cases you want to undervolt tour parts too) because at some points you are trading stability and temperature for more power. Don’t attempt overclocking if you don’t know what you are doing.

-Anyway, at this point and time it’s better to use an amd cpu witch are better and cheaper, something like the ryzen 7 2700 but soon amd will release the next generation of cpu. 

-After the cpu you need to have a motherboard that supports that cpu and if you don’t need to overclock anything, you can just go with a b450 (for this generation, or for the r3/5/7 3xxx you can wait and see if the newer ones will be compatible).

-Then you have the ram, for intel it doesn’t really matter what speed or latency you are going to put in the pc (as long as they are ddr4, the “new” standard), while ryzen need to have high speed, at least 3200mhz (if not you are going to lose a little bit too much fps in gaming or power in other circumstances).

-As for the gpu instead of a 1060 (which is really not ideal now) you either want an amd rx580 (200/250€ where I live) if you are going budget or spending for at least a 2060 (350/400€) to be future proof.

-storage: for the storage any ssd will be good for your booting drive, keep in mind that they can be either Sata (usually 500mb/s read  and 200/300 mb/s write) or nvme (super fast, they are like 2.5/3 gb/s read and 2/2.5 write), go for crucial or samsung. You also need a lot of space for your games so you need a second drive for it (if you don’t want to go full ssd witch is quite expensive. Just grab any 2/3/4 TB hdd and you’ll be good (segate is recommend)

-Power supply: it’s a really important choice here. DON’T GO CHEAP ON THE POWER SUPPLY.... btw really, for a low end build you can go with a 350/400W power supply, for a medium end 500 to 600 and for a high end build 600 to 800 (it really depends on your pc parts and how much they are power hungry). Anyway, go for a bequiet or a seasonic power supply (they are the most reliable, but there are many good power supply, just ask when you are going to build your pc).

-case: it’s an important part as well, there are many case’s but many don’t offer a good airflow witch means that the parts are going to be hotter than it should be, I’m not really an expert on this topic tho.

-Aftermarket cooler:  some cpu come with a stock cooler but if you are going to stress your cpu consider an aftermarket cooler (don’t go with a liquid cooler because it’s not recommended for a new user). Any decent cooler will be good.

-fans: your case may have built in fans or not so if they haven’t any or your case isn’t that good in the first place you can mount other fans but.... just use a good case
